page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.metal-48xl is a storage-optimized bare-metal server powered by 192 dedicated physical cores of AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors running at 2.7 GHz. The architecture is arm64 with single-threaded cores, meaning there is no hyperthreading. It features 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For storage, it includes a massive 120,000 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a 300 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

In benchmark testing, the i8ge.metal-48xl demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU and memory performance. The multi-core stress-ng score reaches 287,164.37, and the multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed is 1,270.14 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with cached small-block reads at 13,947.51 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 897.06 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET performance are also in the top tier, with Redis handling 378.59 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is average, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,666.0, and LLM text generation performance is poor, with only 28.16 tokens per second on a small model.

Given its bare-metal status, high resource density, and massive local NVMe storage, this server offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring high-throughput local data access without network storage overhead. The lack of hyperthreading ensures predictable, dedicated core performance. It is highly suited for large-scale databases, high-performance cache layers like Redis, data-intensive storage applications, and parallelized multi-core tasks such as software compilation. It is less suitable for workloads dependent on high single-thread performance or GPU acceleration.
